page: Microsoft Azure M64bds_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the MBDSMediumMemoryv3 family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8473C x86_64 processor featuring 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a clock speed of 4.0 GHz and includes a 105 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 512.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided via a 410 GB disk, and the instance is premium storage capable. No GPU accelerators are present on this server.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong performance characteristics across multiple domains. The server demonstrates top-tier capabilities in image processing and strong results in memory bandwidth, with read-only large block bandwidth reaching 217.42 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth at 92.79 GB/sec. Computational benchmarks show strong multi-core performance, with Geekbench multi-core scores and Passmark CPU scores ranking in the top 25 percent. Cryptographic and vector operations benefit from advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the M64bds_v3 offers a dense memory-to-vCPU allocation that is optimized for memory-bound workloads without the overhead of a larger vCPU footprint. This resource balance makes it highly suitable for hosting large relational databases, in-memory caches like Redis, and enterprise applications. It is also well-suited for software compilation, text processing, and medium-scale language model inference tasks, where its high memory bandwidth and dedicated Intel Xeon cores provide consistent, predictable performance.
description: Microsoft Azure M64bds_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the MBDSMediumMemoryv3 family, designed for memory-intensive enterprise workloads. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8473C x86_64 processor, it features 64 dedicated vCPUs running at 4.0 GHz, 512.0 GB of RAM, and a 410 GB local disk. The server lacks GPU acceleration but delivers strong benchmark results, particularly in memory bandwidth, database operations, and image processing. Advanced instruction support, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX, enhances its computational efficiency. The M64bds_v3 is highly suited for large-scale databases, in-memory caching, software compilation, and medium-scale LLM inference tasks.
